quests.hint: Judgement about faults or merits. It comes from 'critic', but the c near the end sounds different from the first one.
quests.explanation: Critic + ism: the first c says /k/ and the second, before i, says /s/. Both are written c, so 'critisism' is wrong.

quests.hint: Attention from the media. It comes from the adjective 'public', and the spelling of its c does not change even though the sound does.
quests.explanation: Public + ity: the c stays, but its sound shifts from /k/ to /s/, as in electric to electricity. The spelling doesn't change with the sound.

quests.hint: Someone who works in government. The ending names a person, and the /ʃ/ sound comes after a c.
quests.explanation: Politic + ian: the c before -ian says /ʃ/, giving -cian, the same as in musician and technician.

quests.hint: Worth a lot. The base 'value' ends in e, and this adjective drops it.
quests.explanation: Value + able loses the e: valuable. Do not write 'valueable'; the e drops before a vowel suffix.

quests.hint: Easy to see or spot. The base ends in e, and this adjective keeps it.
quests.explanation: Notice + able keeps the e, because a soft c needs an e or i after it. Many writers drop the e and produce 'noticable'.

quests.hint: Able to be powered up again. The verb inside keeps its e so that the g stays soft.
quests.explanation: Re + charge + able keeps the e, exactly as in changeable and noticeable. Without it, 'rechargable' would suggest a hard g.

quests.hint: Brave. The ending is -eous, and there is an e right after the g.
quests.explanation: Courage + ous keeps the e so the g stays soft, giving /dʒ/. The same happens in outrageous and advantageous.

quests.hint: Shockingly extreme or unacceptable. It ends in -eous after a g.
quests.explanation: Outrage + ous keeps its e after the g, for the same reason as courageous. The soft g needs it.

quests.hint: Very beautiful. The g is soft, and the ending is -eous.
quests.explanation: Gor-geous has geous, said /dʒəs/. It is not built from a base word, so its e cannot be explained by a rule and must be learned.

quests.hint: Careful examination of something. It has a y in the middle and ends in -sis.
quests.explanation: A-nal-y-sis has y, from Greek, in the third chunk, and it ends in -sis. The plural changes -sis to -ses: analyses.

quests.hint: Books, poems and plays as a subject. The ending is -ture, and the first chunk has a single t.
quests.explanation: Lit-er-a-ture has four chunks and ends in -ture, said /tʃə/. It is related to literate, and the stress is on the first syllable.

quests.hint: A summary of what a course covers. The first syllable has a y, and the ending is -us.
quests.explanation: Syl-la-bus has y in the first syllable, as in syllable, and a double l. The plural is syllabuses or syllabi.

quests.hint: A plan to reach a goal. The ending is /dʒi/, and a weak middle vowel is easy to skip.
quests.explanation: Strat-e-gy has an e in the middle that is barely heard. The ending -gy says /dʒi/, as in energy and biology.

quests.hint: To reach agreement by discussion. The ti says /ʃ/, and the ending is -ate.
quests.explanation: Ne-go-ti-ate has ti for /ʃ/ in the third chunk, and ends in -ate. The noun form, negotiation, drops the e.

quests.hint: Working well without wasting effort. It begins with a double f, and the /ʃ/ sound is spelled ci.
quests.explanation: Ef-fi-cient has ff, from the prefix ex- meeting fic, and -cient says /ʃənt/. The ending is the same as in ancient.

quests.hint: Roughly. It has a double p, and the ending is -ately.
quests.explanation: Ap-prox-i-mate-ly has pp from the prefix ad- and keeps the e of -ate before -ly. The last chunk is -ately, said /ətli/.

quests.hint: Enough. It begins with a double f, and the ending is -cient.
quests.explanation: Suf-fi-cient has ff, because the prefix sub- becomes suf- before f. The ending -cient, said /ʃənt/, matches efficient.

quests.hint: To obtain something. The /k/ sound is written with two different letters, and the ending has a silent e.
quests.explanation: Ac-quire has cq for /k/, in the same way as in acquaint. The prefix ac- meets quire, and the final e is silent.

quests.hint: The act of tricking someone. Its verb ends in -ceive, and the noun changes the v.
quests.explanation: Deceive becomes deception: the v turns into p and ei becomes e. Perceive and conceive give perception and conception in the same way.

quests.hint: Something taken as true without proof. The verb 'assume' gains a p.
quests.explanation: Assume becomes assumption: a p appears between m and t. Consume works the same way: consumption.

quests.hint: An account of what something is like. The verb 'describe' turns its b into p.
quests.explanation: Describe becomes description: b turns into p, as in prescribe and prescription. The ending is -tion, not -sion.

quests.hint: A result. It ends in -ence, and the qu says /kw/.
quests.explanation: Con-se-quence ends in -quence. The letters qu are always together, and the final -ence is the more common of the two endings.

quests.hint: A duty you are bound to fulfil. Its verb ends in -ige, and the g sounds different in the noun.
quests.explanation: Oblige becomes obligation: the e drops and -ation is added, and the g hardens from /dʒ/ to /g/. The spelling keeps the g both times.

quests.hint: A condition surrounding an event. The prefix means 'around'.
quests.explanation: Circum (around) + stance (standing): circumstance. The prefix also appears in circumference. The ending is -ance.

quests.hint: A line of people waiting. It has five letters, and four are vowels.
quests.explanation: Queue is pronounced /kjuː/, so the letters ueue after q are silent. It is one of the few words with such a long vowel string.

quests.hint: A space with no air. There are two u's in a row.
quests.explanation: Vac-u-um has uu, which is unusual in English. It comes from the Latin vacuus, meaning empty.

quests.hint: Someone you know slightly. It has cq and ends in -ance.
quests.explanation: Ac-quaint-ance has cq, as in acquire, and ends in -ance. The base is acquaint, and the ending is -ance: 'acquaintence' is wrong.

quests.hint: Someone who starts a business. It is a French word, and it ends in -eur.
quests.explanation: En-tre-pre-neur keeps its French spelling: entre (between) and prendre (to take). The ending -eur is said /ɜː/, so the sound gives little help with the letters.

quests.hint: Of various kinds. It has five syllables and ends in -eous.
quests.explanation: Mis-cel-la-ne-ous has sc in the middle, a double l and ends in -aneous. The tempting wrong form is 'miscellanious'.

quests.hint: Training and self-control. Like 'science', it has sc where you hear /s/.
quests.explanation: Dis-ci-pline has sci, said /si/, just as science does. The word is spelled with a c after the s.
